name: Augustin Reyes-Mbatha
role: Street-level medic and unlicensed augmentation surgeon operating out of Old Harbor
description:
Augustin is a broad-shouldered man whose face has been mapped by decades of difficult living — deep-set creases around his eyes, a jaw that still carries the ghost of old muscle, skin the warm brown of river silt that has seen too many winters. His hair is close-cropped and almost entirely white, though his eyebrows remain stubbornly dark, giving him an expression of permanent mild surprise. He works in a converted barge permanently moored at Canal 7, where the smell of antiseptic and frying oil from the neighbouring food stall have become inseparable. His hands are his most striking feature: enormous, steady, and threaded with the fine silver filaments of a haptic-feedback augmentation that lets him feel at the microscopic level — installed, he'll tell anyone who asks, by himself, on himself, without anaesthetic, in 2171.

He was once a licensed trauma surgeon at a Meridian Core hospital before a malpractice suit — widely believed to have been engineered by a corporate competitor — stripped him of his credentials and left him with a debt load that pushed him to the Shelf and eventually to Old Harbor. He rebuilt himself slowly, earning trust one stitched wound at a time, one extracted bullet at a time, until the canal district came to regard him as something between a doctor and a priest. He charges what people can pay, which is often very little, and he has never turned away a patient who was bleeding.

Augustin carries his past with the careful stillness of a man who has decided not to be destroyed by it, but has not quite decided to forgive it either. He drinks a single glass of real Scotch every evening at precisely 8 p.m. — a ritual that functions simultaneously as reward, mourning, and punctuation. He keeps a photograph of his daughter, Liria, tucked under the lip of his operating lamp. She is in The Spire now, a junior executive at Helix-Vantage Biomedical. They have not spoken in eleven years.

core_fears: That his competence will one day fail someone who trusted him completely
That Liria has become exactly what the system that destroyed him wanted her to become
That his exile from medicine was partly deserved — that he was arrogant, and the system only named it
core_desires: To practice medicine with full resources, just once more, without apology
A reconciliation with Liria that does not require either of them to lie
To see Old Harbor become a place where people do not have to choose between eating and healing
coping_mechanisms: Radical focus on the immediate task — when working, nothing else exists
Dark, self-deprecating humour deployed before anyone else can aim it at him
Maintaining strict daily routines as proof of personal order amid external chaos
Mentorship — teaching what he knows to anyone willing to learn
blind_spots: Mistakes stubbornness for principle, sometimes to the detriment of patients who need referral
Underestimates how much his martyrdom narrative shapes his choices
Cannot see that some people in Old Harbor rely on his presence so heavily it has become a form of dependency he enables
psychology.secret: The malpractice suit was not entirely fabricated. Augustin made an error — a small one, non-fatal, but real — and rather than disclose it, he let the corporate narrative swallow it whole. He has never told anyone. The patient lived. He isn't sure that matters.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Medical precision mixed with the worn idioms of someone who has lived in many cities; occasional Spanish phrases, especially under stress; avoids corporate jargon with visible distaste
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate when explaining, faster and clipped when working; capable of long, winding sentences that arrive at their point only after establishing every surrounding condition
verbal_tics: "You follow me?" — used to check comprehension, not condescend
A habit of naming the body part before describing what he's doing to it
Starts disagreements with "Now—" and a brief pause
example_lines: "Now — I hear what you're saying, and I respect it, but your spleen is not interested in your ideology right now."
"The liver's taken worse. Probably. Lie still."
"You follow me? Good. Because I'm going to need you conscious for the next part and it would help if you trusted me."
"I've been past the door three times on the table and twice off it. I know what it looks like. You're not there yet. Hold on."
"She works for Helix-Vantage. My daughter. No, I don't want to talk about it. Hold the light steady."

relationships.name: Liria Reyes-Mbatha
relationships.description: Junior executive at Helix-Vantage Biomedical in The Spire; has not contacted Augustin in eleven years
relationships.emotional_core: A grief he has categorised as resolved and visits nightly
relationships.story_tension: Liria may be involved in a Helix-Vantage project that will directly affect Old Harbor patients; the plot may force contact neither of them has prepared for

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.description: Sable occasionally routes injured contacts to Augustin's barge; Augustin treats them without asking questions he doesn't want answered
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual respect built on shared commitment to not letting people die unnecessarily; neither fully trusts the other's methods
relationships.story_tension: Sable's work keeps bringing patients whose injuries suggest an escalating conflict Augustin is being kept deliberately ignorant of

relationships.name: Perpetua Okafor
relationships.description: Perpetua has sent community members to Augustin and occasionally consults him on health conditions in her district; they share a background of institutional betrayal
relationships.emotional_core: Recognition — two people who see the shape of each other's losses without needing them explained
relationships.story_tension: Perpetua knows something about the original malpractice case that Augustin does not, and hasn't decided whether telling him would help or destroy him

story_hooks: A patient arrives with an augmentation Augustin has never seen — proprietary, deeply embedded, and actively resisting removal — and the person who installed it is hunting the patient
Liria contacts Augustin through an intermediary with a job offer that is clearly also a surveillance operation; he doesn't know whether she's warning him or baiting him
A series of Old Harbor residents are presenting with identical neurological symptoms; Augustin begins to suspect the water filtration system has been tampered with, and the tampering is recent
A young medic apprentice Augustin has been training is offered a corporate scholarship — the same institution that destroyed his career — and asks his advice

Evidence surfaces that the patient from his original malpractice case has been found dead, the circumstances pointing to deliberate silencing, and someone is leaving that information where Augustin will find it
narrative_function: Moral anchor and threshold guardian for the street-level world; represents the cost of integrity in a system designed to monetise suffering; his barge functions as a neutral ground where information and people converge
augmentations: Haptic-feedback microsurgical filaments in both hands (self-installed, uncertified),Subdermal toxin-analysis patch on left forearm — identifies contaminants on contact,Optical overlay for vein and tissue mapping, left eye only (right eye refused on principle),Cervical pain-suppression node — installed to manage a spinal injury, kept because the work requires it
daily_life: Wakes at 5 a.m. regardless of when he slept, makes strong coffee in a battered press, reviews any overnight patients. Mornings are walk-in hours; afternoons are appointments, teaching, or supply runs through Old Harbor's grey market. Evenings are for complex procedures requiring controlled conditions. The 8 p.m. Scotch is inviolable. Sleeps in a hammock strung across the barge's bow cabin, often with a medical text open on his chest.
affiliation: Independent; loosely aligned with Old Harbor's informal mutual aid networks; explicitly unaffiliated with any corporate or government body

stress.response: Retreats into procedural focus, humor becomes darker

decision_rules: Will never turn away a bleeding patient regardless of faction or ability to pay
Will always explain a procedure before performing it, even under fire
Will never refer a patient to a corporate facility unless death is the alternative
Will always maintain the 8 p.m. Scotch ritual — it is the last structure holding him together
Will never discuss Liria voluntarily — the subject is closed until she opens it
Will always teach anyone willing to learn, even at cost to his own schedule
Will never accept payment he considers disproportionate to the patient's means
escalation_ladder: Self-deprecating deflection — humor to lower the temperature
Clinical detachment — treats the conflict like a diagnosis, names the problem precisely
Quiet, immovable refusal — 'Now—' followed by a boundary that will not move
Deploys the authority of thirty years of trauma medicine — voice drops, hands steady, the room obeys
Walks away entirely and does not look back — his final escalation is absence

interpersonal_modes.Liria: Avoidant grief masked as acceptance; keeps her photo where he works as penance
interpersonal_modes.Sable: Professional courtesy stretched thin over mutual suspicion; treats Sable's people without asking questions
interpersonal_modes.Perpetua Okafor: Quiet recognition — two institutional refugees who share losses without naming them
interpersonal_modes.Patients: Warm authority — the doctor-priest hybrid Old Harbor needs

stress_responses.low: Maintains routines with extra precision, coffee gets stronger
stress_responses.medium: Spanish phrases surface, humor sharpens to a cutting edge
stress_responses.high: Goes silent except for clinical communication, works until his hands shake
stress_responses.critical: The old arrogance resurfaces — he becomes the Meridian Core surgeon again, brilliant and terrifying

contradictions: Teaches honesty in medicine while concealing the truth about his malpractice case
Refuses corporate medicine on principle while his cervical implant keeps him functional
Creates dependency in Old Harbor while believing he empowers self-sufficiency
habits: Makes coffee in a battered press at 5 a.m. regardless of sleep
Names the body part aloud before touching it during examination
Checks on Liria's photograph under the operating lamp at the start of each procedure
Walks the barge deck once before any complex surgery
Pours the 8 p.m. Scotch with his left hand — always the left
breaking_points: A patient dying because he lacked resources he once had access to
Liria appearing in person, unannounced, on the barge
The original malpractice error becoming public knowledge in Old Harbor
Being forced to choose between two patients when only one can be saved
